title.narrative: Integrated Multi-Sectoral Life-Saving Response for IDPs in Shire and Sheraro, Northwest Tigray Region

description.narrative: ltpgtltspangtConflict-induced displacement in Tigray has left thousands of IDPs and vulnerable host communities in Shire and Sheraro living in substandard conditions with limited access to essential services. Displacement of personnel has resulted in overcrowded collective sites and informal settlements, exposing IDPs to heightened protection risks, including gender-based violence (GBV), psychosocial distress, and poor hygiene conditions. Rapid assessments conducted by NMWEO and Medical Teams International (MTI), together with cluster priority reviews and consultations, IN prepared a response plan on multi-sectoral needs requiring a coordinated humanitarian response.lt/spangtlt/pgtltpgtltspangtltbrgtlt/spangtlt/pgtltpgtThe project targets six IDP sites, three in Shire and three in Sheraro selected based on assessment findings, cluster priorities, and available budget. The intervention adopts a multi-sectoral approach covering ES/NFI, WASH, Protection, CCCM, Health, and Nutrition. In ES/NFI, emergency shelter kits and rental support will provide safe, dignified living conditions, while CCCM activities strengthen site management, coordination, and community participation. Site decommissioning will also be supported under CCCM to ensure safe transitions for displaced populations.lt/pgtltpgtltbrgtWASH interventions will address critical sanitation and hygiene gaps by rehabilitating existing facilities, constructing semi-permanent WASH facilities and WASH NFIs, and implementing hygiene promotion campaigns. These measures will reduce disease risks and improve overall wellbeing in IDP sites. Health and nutrition interventions, implemented with MTI, will include deployment of mobile health and nutrition teams in Sheraro and support to Shire health facilities through a Health System Strengthening (HSS) approach. Services include primary healthcare, maternal and child health, outpatient therapeutic programs for severe acute malnutrition, nutrition education, infant and young child feeding (IYCF) counseling, deworming, and community health promotion activities.lt/pgtltpgtltbrgtProtection interventions include general protection and GBV-specific activities. Cash and voucher assistance (CVA) will be integrated to reduce negative coping mechanisms among households, while GBV response support will cover transportation, medical care, and legal assistance for survivors. The approach complements services provided by CSOs scheduled to phase out in December, ensuring continuity, filling gaps, and prioritizing support to the most vulnerable households.lt/pgtltpgtltbrgtThe project adopts a locally led, gender-responsive, and cost-effective approach. By integrating multi-sectoral interventions, it ensures alignment with cluster priorities and existing humanitarian frameworks, strengthens community-based protection, improves access to essential services, and promotes accountability and participation. This coordinated approach directly contributes to the EHF 2025 strategic objectives of delivering principled, timely, and impactful humanitarian assistance while supporting sustainable recovery and resilience for affected populations.lt/pgtltpgtltbrgtProject Objectives:lt/pgtltpgtltbrgt1. Provide safe, dignified, and functional shelter and rental support for IDPs.ltbrgt2. Rehabilitate and construct WASH facilities, provide WASH NFIs, hygiene promotion, and desludging services.ltbrgt3. Deliver lifesaving health and nutrition services, including maternal and child health, malnutrition treatment, and community nutrition education.ltbrgt4. Strengthen general protection and GBV response, integrating CVA to reduce negative coping mechanisms and providing transportation, medical, and legal support for survivors.ltbrgt5. Enhance site management, coordination, and community engagement through CCCM activities, including site decommissioning where applicable.ltbrgtltbrgtlt/pgtltpgtThrough this integrated, multi-sectoral, and locally led response, the project will ensure that IDPs in Shire and Sheraro receive timely, comprehensiveltspangt, and sustainable humanitarian assistance, addressing immediate needs while promoting longer-term resilience and recovery.lt/spangtlt/pgt
